process.name: KYC and customer onboarding
process.owner: Retail onboarding and Financial Crime Compliance

objective: Open accounts for eligible individual customers within minutes, after verifying identity, screening for sanctions and PEP exposure and rating financial-crime risk, with a recorded rationale for every outcome.

in_scope: Individual customers aged 18 or over, resident in the bank's home country
Applications through the mobile app, the website or a branch
out_of_scope: Periodic KYC refresh of existing customers

triggers: An applicant submits an account opening application in the mobile app, on the website or in a branch

actors.name: Applicant
responsibilities: Provide the application, an identity document, proof of address and a selfie video

actors.name: KYC analyst
responsibilities: Obtain senior approval for PEP and high-risk customers

actors.name: Money Laundering Reporting Officer
responsibilities: Decide whether to file a suspicious activity report
Decide whether the relationship can proceed after a suspicion

actors.name: Identity verification provider
responsibilities: Check document authenticity, liveness and face match

actors.name: Sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening provider
responsibilities: Screen the applicant against sanctions, PEP and adverse media lists

actors.name: Customer risk rating engine
responsibilities: Score customer risk from the risk factors in the KYC policy

actors.name: Core banking system
responsibilities: Create the customer and the account

stages.name: Application capture
stages.purpose: Extract applicant details from the application and documents, check eligibility and completeness, record biometric consent and check for an existing customer record.

decision.question: Can the application be processed? Evaluated in order; the first matching outcome wins.

outcomes.label: out_of_scope
outcomes.condition: customer_profile.customer_type is not individual, or customer_profile.country_of_residence is not the home country, or customer_profile.age < 18

outcomes.label: incomplete
outcomes.condition: customer_profile.missing_documents is not empty, or customer_profile.consent_biometrics is false

stages.notes: An existing customer found in the CRM is linked, not duplicated; their existing risk rating is passed on in customer_profile.existing_risk_band.

stages.name: Identity document verification
stages.purpose: Check that the identity document is genuine and in date, that the selfie is live and matches the document photo, and that the address is verified.

decision.question: Is the identity verified? Evaluated in order; the first matching outcome wins.

outcomes.label: refer
outcomes.condition: idv_result.document_authentic is false, or idv_result.liveness_passed is false, or idv_result.face_match_score < 0.90, or idv_result.address_verified is false, or idv_result.document_expired is true

stages.notes: A failed check is never auto-rejected: a person decides, because a forged document may be a fraud case the applicant must not be told about.

stages.name: Sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening
stages.purpose: Screen the verified applicant against sanctions, politically exposed person and adverse media lists.

decision.question: Is the applicant clear of screening alerts? Evaluated in order; the first matching outcome wins.

outcomes.label: clear
outcomes.condition: Otherwise (PEP matches continue to risk rating, which routes them to enhanced due diligence)

stages.notes: Matches scoring 60-84 are recorded in screening_result.possible_matches for the analyst but do not stop the application on their own.

stages.name: Customer risk rating
stages.purpose: Score financial-crime risk from country, occupation, product, channel, expected activity and PEP status, and decide whether straight-through approval is allowed. A calculation, no model.

decision.question: Which due diligence does the customer need? Evaluated in order; the first matching outcome wins.

outcomes.label: high_risk
outcomes.condition: risk_assessment.risk_score >= 70, or screening_result.pep_match is true, or risk_assessment.country_risk is high

stages.notes: Risk bands: low < 40, medium 40-69, high >= 70. The country risk list comes from the knowledge source 'Country risk list'.

stages.name: Enhanced due diligence
stages.purpose: For PEP and high-risk customers, collect and summarise source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence for the analyst.

decision.question: Is the evidence enough for a review?

stages.sla: < 1 working day, excluding time waiting for the applicant
stages.notes: Reached only from risk_rating (high_risk). The agent summarises evidence; it never decides.

stages.name: KYC analyst review
stages.purpose: Decide applications referred by verification, screening or enhanced due diligence, with senior approval for PEP and high-risk customers, and record the reasons.
stages.notes: Reached from document_verification (refer), screening (alert) or enhanced_due_diligence (evidence_complete). risk_assessment and edd_report exist only on the later paths.

stages.name: MLRO referral
stages.purpose: Decide whether to file a suspicious activity report and whether the relationship may proceed.
stages.notes: Reached only from kyc_review (report_suspicion). SAR filing itself happens in the bank's reporting system, outside this workflow; only the decision and reference are recorded.

stages.name: Account opening
stages.purpose: Create the customer and the account in core banking, with the transaction-monitoring tier set from the risk rating.
stages.notes: Reached from risk_rating (standard), kyc_review (approve) or mlro_referral (proceed). Refuses to run unless kyc_decision.outcome is approve.

stages.name: Welcome communication
stages.purpose: Send the welcome message with account details, card delivery and next steps. Ends the run.
stages.sla: < 5 minutes after the account is opened
stages.notes: Sent on the channel the applicant used, plus email.

stages.name: Notify applicant
stages.purpose: Tell the applicant what happens next: the documents or evidence still needed, why the application is out of scope, or that it cannot proceed. Ends the run.
stages.notes: Reached from application_capture, enhanced_due_diligence, kyc_review (reject) and mlro_referral (exit_relationship). After an MLRO exit the notice uses neutral wording and gives no reason. A resubmission starts a new run.

business.description: No account is opened until identity is verified and the applicant has been screened.
A possible sanctions match scoring 85 or more is never cleared automatically; a KYC analyst decides it.
PEP and high-risk customers get enhanced due diligence and senior management approval before an account is opened.
Every customer gets a recorded risk rating with the factors that produced it, and the monitoring tier follows the rating.
When a suspicion is reported, the applicant is not told: notices after an MLRO exit use neutral wording and give no reason.
Every approve, refer, reject and exit records who decided and the reasons.
Customer due diligence records are kept for at least five years after the relationship ends.
The applicant gives explicit consent to biometric processing before the selfie video is used.

technical.description: Identity verification and screening calls time out after 20 seconds and retry twice; after that the application is referred, never passed.
Screening runs against lists updated within the last 24 hours; the list version date is stored with each result.
Every agent stage returns JSON matching its data entity; an output that does not match fails the step.
Names, dates of birth, document numbers and addresses are masked in logs and run traces.
Selfie video and document images are deleted from platform storage within 30 days of the decision; only the verification result is kept.
Account creation uses the application id as an idempotency key, so a retry cannot open a second account.

exceptions.condition: The identity document, proof of address or selfie video is missing, or biometric consent was not given
exceptions.handling: List what is missing in customer_profile.missing_documents and route to notify_applicant; do not verify.

exceptions.condition: The identity provider cannot read the document image
exceptions.handling: Refer to a KYC analyst, who can ask the applicant to upload it again; never treat it as verified.

exceptions.condition: The identity or screening provider does not answer after the retries in vendor_timeout_fallback
exceptions.handling: Refer to a KYC analyst with the reason; never treat a missing result as clear.

exceptions.condition: The document looks forged, the selfie fails liveness, or the identity is already linked to fraud
exceptions.handling: Refer to a KYC analyst; tell the applicant nothing about the reason.

exceptions.condition: Source-of-funds or source-of-wealth evidence is missing for a PEP or high-risk customer
exceptions.handling: Ask the applicant for the listed evidence through notify_applicant; do not review or open the account.

risks.description: A sanctioned person is given an account.
risks.mitigation: sanctions_no_auto_clear and screening_list_freshness; no account opens before screening (cdd_before_account).

risks.description: An account is opened with a forged or synthetic identity.
risks.mitigation: Document authenticity, liveness and face match must all pass; any failure goes to an analyst.

risks.description: A notice reveals to the applicant that a suspicion was reported.
risks.mitigation: no_tipping_off; the notice reviewer checks the wording of every notice after an MLRO exit.

risks.description: Selfie videos or document images leak from platform storage.
risks.mitigation: biometric_data_deletion and pii_masked_in_logs; images are stored encrypted in the bank's region only.

risks.description: Applicants abandon onboarding because it takes too long or asks for documents repeatedly.
risks.mitigation: Ask for every missing item in one notice; track the drop-off KPI.

regulations.name: Anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing
regulations.requirement: Identify and verify customers, apply a risk-based approach with enhanced due diligence for PEPs and high-risk customers, keep records, report suspicions and do not tip off (FATF Recommendations 10, 11, 12, 20 and 21).

regulations.name: Financial sanctions
regulations.requirement: Do not provide services to designated persons; screen before onboarding and resolve possible matches before opening an account.

regulations.name: Data protection
regulations.requirement: Process personal and biometric data only with a lawful basis and explicit consent for biometrics, minimise what is kept and protect it in storage and logs.

data_entities.name: customer_profile
fields: customer_type (one of: individual, business, charity, trust)
existing_risk_band (one of: low, medium, high, none)
missing_documents (list of strings, empty when complete)

data_entities.name: idv_result
fields: face_match_score (number, 0-1, higher is a closer match)

data_entities.name: screening_result
fields: pep_category (one of: none, domestic, foreign, international_organisation, family_or_associate)

data_entities.name: edd_report
fields: evidence_gaps (list of strings, empty when complete)
pep_details (string, empty when not a PEP)

data_entities.name: kyc_decision
fields: outcome (one of: approve, refer, reject, report_suspicion, exit)
senior_approval_by (string, required for PEP and high-risk approvals)

data_entities.name: applicant_notice
fields: reason (one of: missing_documents, out_of_scope, edd_evidence_missing, rejected, relationship_declined)

business.name: Straight-through onboarding rate
business.target: >= 70% of complete applications opened with no human review
business.description: Share of applications approved by policy rules alone.

business.name: Time to open an account
business.target: < 10 minutes for straight-through applications; < 2 working days for reviewed ones

business.name: Application drop-off
business.description: Applicants who never complete after a notice asking for documents or evidence.

business.name: Analyst review within SLA
business.target: >= 95% of referrals decided within 1 working day

business.name: Screening false-positive rate
business.target: < 5% of screened applications raise an alert that is cleared
business.description: Far above target means the match threshold needs tuning.

technical.name: Automated path duration
technical.target: p95 < 3 minutes from submission to the risk rating
technical.description: Excludes time waiting for people or the applicant.

technical.name: Vendor call success
technical.description: Identity verification and screening calls together.

technical.name: Valid structured outputs
technical.target: >= 99% of agent outputs match their data entity on the first attempt
technical.description: Failures are retried once, then the step fails.

technical.name: Model cost per application
technical.description: Model calls only; vendor fees are tracked separately.

recommendation.title: Straight-through KYC onboarding with analyst review for exceptions
recommendation.pain_point: Every application is checked by hand, which takes 3-5 days, and about a third of applicants abandon before their account is opened.

intervention.description: Agents extract data, assemble due diligence evidence and write communications; vendors verify and screen; rules rate risk and approve standard cases; people decide every exception.

evidence.source: Interviews with the onboarding team and six months of application data

value.expected_benefits: Most applications opened in minutes instead of days, lower drop-off, and analysts focused on the referred minority.

drivers: Identity verification and screening vendors with APIs are already contracted
The KYC policy already defines risk factors and thresholds
assumptions: About 70% of applications are low or medium risk with no screening alert
Core banking exposes an account-creation API
constraints: Biometric data must stay in the bank's region
Model risk approval is needed before go-live

trigger.source: Mobile app, website or branch tablet

third_party_services.name: Identity verification service
third_party_services.purpose: Document authenticity, liveness, face match and address verification
third_party_services.fallback: Refer to a KYC analyst for manual document checks

third_party_services.name: Sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening
third_party_services.purpose: Screen applicants against sanctions, PEP and adverse media lists
third_party_services.fallback: Refer to a KYC analyst, who screens in the vendor's web portal

sources.name: KYC and customer due diligence policy
sources.location: Policy library / Financial crime / KYC policy v7

sources.name: Country risk list
sources.location: Financial crime data mart, table country_risk

input_artifacts.name: onboarding_application
input_artifacts.source: Mobile app, website or branch tablet

output_artifacts.name: kyc_file
output_artifacts.destination: Financial crime case management, retained for 5 years after the relationship ends

data.residency: All personal and biometric data stays in the bank's home region

sub_agents.name: Application capture agent
sub_agents.role: Extract and check application and document data

sub_agents.name: EDD research agent
sub_agents.role: Assemble and summarise source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence

sub_agents.name: Customer communications agent
sub_agents.role: Write welcome messages and applicant notices

sub_agents.name: Notice reviewer
sub_agents.role: Check every notice against no_tipping_off before it is sent

agent_design.mapping_rationale: Steps are fixed and decisions are rules or people, so agents only extract, summarise and write. Notices need a reflective check because a wrong word can tip off a suspect.

risk.reason: Financial-crime controls on personal and biometric data; a miss can onboard a sanctioned person.

human_oversight.threshold: Every verification referral, screening alert and PEP or high-risk customer; plus a QA sample of straight-through approvals

criteria: Every account has a verified identity, a screening result and a risk rating
Every decision records who decided and why
No notice after an MLRO exit contains a reason
validation.accuracy_threshold: >= 98% agreement between straight-through approvals and analyst decisions on the QA sample

segregation_of_duties: The analyst who decides a referral cannot be the one who gives senior approval for it.
Only the MLRO decides whether a suspicious activity report is filed.
governance_controls: Monthly review of risk-rating thresholds by Financial Crime Compliance
Quarterly QA sample report to the MLRO
Model risk approval before go-live and after any model change

operations.fallback_mode: Route every application to manual KYC review in case management

glossary.KYC: Know your customer: verifying who a customer is and understanding their financial-crime risk.
glossary.CDD: Customer due diligence: identifying and verifying the customer and understanding the purpose of the relationship.
glossary.EDD: Enhanced due diligence: extra checks, including source of funds and wealth, for PEPs and high-risk customers.
glossary.PEP: Politically exposed person: someone with a prominent public function, or their family or close associates.
glossary.MLRO: Money Laundering Reporting Officer: the person who decides on suspicious activity reports.
glossary.SAR: Suspicious activity report, filed with the financial intelligence unit.
glossary.Tipping off: Telling someone that a suspicion about them has been reported or is being investigated.
glossary.Liveness: A check that the selfie is a live person, not a photo, mask or replay.
glossary.Straight-through: Opened by policy rules with no human review.
